articles.title: Trump administration's social media posts spark criticism over racially charged images
articles.summary: Criticism surrounds the Trump administration's use of social media to highlight its aggressive immigration enforcement and crackdown on alleged fraudsters ahead of the midterm elections.
articles.content: The Trump administration's social media accounts have sparked criticism for circulating images that some deem inflammatory and racially charged in the lead-up to the midterm elections. The posts feature a pumpkin carved with a sombrero design and a fake Halloween-themed background surrounding a Black man who appears to be accused of food assistance fraud. This image is being shared as part of the government's efforts to highlight its aggressive immigration enforcement and crackdown on alleged fraudsters, particularly in relation to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program. The timing of these posts coincides with rising concerns about affordability among voters, with healthcare costs and economic stressors topping the list of voter priorities. The administration has been emphasizing its commitment to saving taxpayers' money through tough action against those accused of defrauding government programs. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins was one of the officials who shared this image on social media platform X over the weekend, posting a photo that includes a headline reading "SNAP FRAUDSTER and a fake Spirit Halloween costume packaging backdrop. A pumpkin carved with a sombrero and the words Spooky szn is here was featured in a White House post on X, sparking renewed criticism of the administration's social media strategy ahead of elections. The image appears to be taken from an Instagram post by Shawty Dred, a social media personality who has been accused of obtaining millions in government benefits through fraudulent means. In September 2025, Shawty Dred posted the photo, which was then shared by Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins on X over the weekend. Shawty Dred's real name is Mercedes Reshard New, and she is currently facing federal charges for allegedly defrauding the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program of more than $4 million in Georgia. This latest controversy surrounding the White House's social media use comes as no surprise to those who have been critical of their online presence. The White House has a history of posting inflammatory images on official government social media accounts, dating back to last year's government shutdown. At that time, they revived a deepfake video featuring House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries in a fake mustache and sombrero, which was widely criticized for its racist undertones. This move was seen as an attempt to politicize the migrant crisis and shift blame onto Democrats, with Jeffries himself describing the meme as bigoted. The video was played on repeat in the White House briefing room before Vice President JD Vance promised to end the practice once the shutdown ended. The Trump administration's focus on immigration issues has led to a surge in anti-immigrant rhetoric, with allegations of fraud being made against several individuals, including U.S. Rep. Ilhan Omar. The investigation into her family's immigration paperwork is ongoing, and federal authorities are examining potential irregularities. In recent weeks, the administration has also taken punitive measures linked to alleged fraud in various states, including California and Minnesota. These actions have been met with criticism from governors of Democratic-led states, who accuse the federal government of targeting their regions for political reasons rather than addressing legitimate issues. Federal prosecutors have charged an individual known as New with operating more than 350 fraudulent SNAP accounts using stolen identities between January 2020 and July 2026. It's alleged that he applied to become an authorized SNAP retailer through his company, Shawty Dred LLC, and used EBT debit cards to extract approximately $4 million from the affected accounts. Posts on New's Instagram account, which boasts over two million followers, showcase his opulent lifestyle, featuring private jets, luxury vehicles, and large sums of cash. The extravagant displays have been highlighted by federal prosecutors as part of their case against him. The lavish lifestyle allegedly funded by social media influencer New's illicit activities has come under scrutiny in his ongoing federal case. New, also known as Shawty Dred," is accused of using funds meant for families in need to support a life of luxury, according to Special Agent Marlo Graham of the FBI Atlanta office. This misuse of resources is part of a larger scheme that has led to numerous charges against New, including mail fraud and aggravated identity theft. New's history with law enforcement dates back several years, with multiple arrests on suspicion of various crimes such as identity theft, insurance fraud, financial transaction card fraud, forgery, and simple assault. articles.title: Ohio State Suffers 30-18 Loss at USC
articles.summary: The Buckeyes' offense struggled to find its footing against USC's defense in a 30-18 loss.
articles.content: Ohio State's offense struggled to find its footing in a 30-18 loss at USC, raising concerns about the team's national championship aspirations. The Buckeyes' offense was expected to be revitalized with a new quarterback under center after Julian Sayin's potential season-ending injury two weeks ago, but that didn't quite materialize against the Trojans. The Ohio State offense was unable to create big plays against USC's defense, which has been one of the Big Ten's worst this season at limiting explosive plays. The Buckeyes' inability to make the most of their opportunities on the field is a worrying sign for a team that had high hopes for the rest of the season. Jeremiah Smith's Heisman campaign took a hit after Ohio State's loss at USC, with his odds slipping to third in the betting market behind two players from Miami. Despite having a productive game against the Trojans, catching 10 passes for 83 yards and one touchdown on 12 targets, Smith's performance was not as impressive as it has been this season. The fact that Smith put up most of his numbers late in the game, when Ohio State was trailing by three scores, is also a concern. It suggests that he may have struggled to make an impact early on, which could be a worrying sign for his chances of winning the Heisman Trophy. Despite being the favorite ahead of Miami's duo of Darian Mensah and Malachi Toney going into the week, Smith's loss at USC has given those two players an opportunity to close the gap in the betting market. The concern is that if Ohio State's offense continues to struggle, it could have a negative impact on Smith's chances of winning the Heisman. The target share suggests that Smith will still have a chance to hold onto his Heisman hopes, but the fact that he was unable to make an impact early in the game against USC's defense is a worrying sign for his campaign. The Buckeyes' offense struggled to find its rhythm against USC's defense, and Jeremiah Smith missed an opportunity to make a significant impact in the game. The team's remaining schedule includes tough opponents such as Oregon, Northwestern, Nebraska, and Michigan, which may limit Smith's chances of finishing strong. Quarterback C.J. Fahey completed 21 passes out of 38 attempts for 260 yards and one touchdown, but his accuracy on long throws was a concern. He mostly relied on short-to-intermediate passes, asking Ohio State's skill players to make plays in space. This approach helped the team move the ball effectively at times. However, Fahey's lack of success throwing deep was evident, particularly when he tried to push the ball downfield. In one instance, Smith had a clear path to a long touchdown but slipped while adjusting to an underthrown pass. The ball sailed over his head, and the opportunity for a big play was lost. The rainy conditions in Los Angeles may have contributed to Fahey's difficulties with accuracy on long throws. Nevertheless, the decline in yards per catch from Smith's average of nearly 19 yards per reception to just 8.3 yards in this game is notable. USC's defense proved to be a challenge for Ohio State's offense, despite being ranked 83rd nationally in allowing passes of 30 yards or more. The Buckeyes' top target, Jeremiah Smith, had his longest catch of the night limited to just 27 yards. Ohio State's shift towards a run-heavy approach is likely a consequence of their struggles with Fahey at quarterback. In an effort to keep him comfortable in the passing game, the team may focus on shorter and intermediate passes rather than taking deep shots down the field. This change in strategy could have significant implications for Smith's Heisman campaign. If Ohio State prioritizes running plays over long passes, it will be harder for Fahey to connect with Smith on deep throws, making it even more difficult for him to put up numbers that keep him in contention for the award. The Buckeyes' next four opponents are all statistically better at preventing explosive pass plays than USC was. This could make it increasingly tough for Ohio State's offense to get into a rhythm and score points consistently, further complicating Smith's chances of staying in the Heisman conversation. Miami's offense is flourishing under the leadership of its star quarterback-receiver duo, who are putting on a show in every game they play. In their recent win over UNC, the combination was unstoppable, with Mensah delivering an impressive 22-for-29 passing performance for 274 yards and three touchdowns. Notably, Toney's seven catches for 75 yards were overshadowed by his two touchdown receptions, including the decisive score that sealed the game in the final minutes. The duo's dominance has cemented their status as a force to be reckoned with in college football. Miami's upcoming matchup against Notre Dame will undoubtedly provide another opportunity for its stars to shine on national television. A strong performance from Mensah and Toney could create a memorable Heisman moment, one that would give them an edge over other contenders. The outcome of the Notre Dame game may also have a significant impact on Jeremiah Smith's chances of winning the Heisman Trophy. If Miami's star duo is able to put up impressive numbers against the Irish defense, it will be a major hurdle for Smith to overcome in his bid to join the exclusive list of receivers who have won the award. The stakes are high for Smith, but he has already made a strong case as one of the best college football players in recent memory. His legacy is secure, regardless of whether he wins the Heisman or not, but if he's going to achieve this particular milestone, it will require him to overcome significant challenges in the games ahead. Jeremiah Smith's path to the Heisman Trophy has become more treacherous following Ohio State's lackluster performance in its recent loss against USC. The Buckeyes' offense struggled significantly under their new quarterback, which will undoubtedly put pressure on Smith and his team. For Smith to regain his top contender status, he needs to see significant improvement from his young quarterback, receive some assistance from the Canes and Irish, and create spectacular plays after the catch with fewer downfield opportunities. While the team is predicted to remain within the top 10, it will have to contend with the losses suffered by other high-ranked teams this weekend. The Hurricanes' wide receiver Malachi Toney was instrumental in their success, finishing with an impressive seven catches for 75 yards and two touchdowns despite his team trailing in the second half. The Trojans' upset victory will undoubtedly propel them back into the AP Top 25 poll. With this win under their belt, USC can now look to build momentum heading into the final stretch of the season. As the college football landscape continues to shift, Sunday's rankings are sure to reflect the dramatic changes that have taken place over the past week. With several teams vying for a spot in the top 25, it will be interesting to see how the pollsters weigh the various performances and losses suffered by these teams. Georgia's convincing win over Florida has cemented its position in the top three, with the Bulldogs now boasting a 7-1 overall record. The team's defense continues to be a major factor in its success, having delivered another strong performance in the Cocktail Party rivalry.
